issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Hy-Nomas fuse groupwise INT8 weight dequantization
issues.body:
## Motivation

Groupwise INT8 linears currently convert the active weight matrix to FP32, multiply by group scales, and cast to the activation dtype before every GEMM. For the Hy-Nomas INT8 DiT, this creates intermediate FP32 tensors and separate GPU launches on each use.

Fuse group-128 INT8-to-BF16 weight preparation into one Triton kernel while preserving FP32 multiplication and the final BF16 rounding. The linear computation remains BF16 GEMM.

## Modifications

- Add and register `quantization.groupwise_int8_dequant` under `sglang.kernels.ops.quantization`. The checked public API accepts contiguous 2-D CUDA INT8 weights and FP32 scales, supports partial final groups and empty tensors, and produces BF16 weights.
- Dispatch eligible NVIDIA CUDA/BF16 group-128 linears to this API. Preserve the existing PyTorch paths for other configurations. Validate groupwise weight metadata during loading; runtime calls use the checked interface without cached validation state.
- Add kernel numerical/contract tests, compile and CUDA Graph coverage, a registered microbenchmark, and Nomas loading/device-move integration coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

### End-to-end Inference: Bitwise Identical

The final checked interface and the preceding validated-fast-path implementation produced **bitwise-identical outputs (zero numerical difference)** throughout the tested end-to-end inference pipeline:

- **All model predictions**
- **Historical KV cache tensors**
- **Final latents for both events**
- **Decoded video pixels before MP4 encoding**

Tested on RTX 4090 D with the official Hy-Nomas INT8 DiT and FP8 VAE: 352×640 resolution, two 40-frame events, eight inference steps, seed 42, and camera motion. Both runs used the same test-only decoder inference-mode workaround.

The fused kernel also matched the original PyTorch dequantization reference **bit for bit** in all tested numerical cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### End-to-end inference

Configuration: RTX 4090 D, official Hy-Nomas distilled INT8 DiT and FP8 VAE, 352×640 resolution, two 40-frame events (80 frames total), eight inference steps per event, seed 42, guidance scale 1, and camera motion. Component CPU offload was enabled; DiT layerwise offload was disabled. Conditioning cache remained enabled, so these are warm repeated-prompt measurements. Both variants used the same test-only decoder inference-mode workaround.

| E2E latency | PyTorch | Fused Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean | 14.335 s | 11.221 s |
| Median | 13.999 s | 11.141 s |
| Range | 12.403–16.938 s | 10.443–12.158 s |
| Sample standard deviation | 2.238 s | 0.728 s |

### Synchronized stage breakdown

| Component | PyTorch mean | Fused Triton mean | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Whole request, diagnostic pass | 12.360 s | 10.990 s | **11.1%** |
| Text encoding, warm cache | 0.025 s | 0.034 s | — |
| Input validation, timestep and latent preparation | 0.003 s | 0.003 s | — |
| DiT denoising | 7.181 s | 5.791 s | **19.4%** |
| VAE decoding | 4.011 s | 4.016 s | Essentially unchanged |
| Outside measured stages | 1.142 s | 1.147 s | Essentially unchanged |

Within DiT, event 1 generation decreased from **3.375 s to 2.600 s**, and event 2 from **3.288 s to 2.673 s**. These are nested measurements, not additional stages to sum into the total. Outside-stage time includes component residency/transfer work, scheduling/IPC, output saving and other overhead; it is not a pure transfer measurement.

The improvement is concentrated in DiT denoising. The synchronized pass shows a smaller whole-request reduction than the ordinary timing pass, so both results are reported rather than attributing the entire noisier E2E difference to the kernel. The GPU was idle before the experiment; other GPUs and host resources remained shared.

### Dequantization microbenchmark

Measured separately on an initially idle RTX 4090 D; latency in microseconds:

| Weight shape | PyTorch | Fused Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 × 2048 | 41.65 | 13.93 |
| 8192 × 2048 | 310.38 | 55.97 |
| 2048 × 8192 | 310.58 | 55.97 |
| 12288 × 2048 | 516.65 | 83.91 |

The benchmark uses CUDA Graph replay and rotates inputs and outputs to avoid repeated hot-L2 output reuse. The PyTorch reference performs FP32 conversion/multiplication and copies into a preallocated BF16 output. These measurements exclude BF16 GEMM and Python submission overhead. Separate eager measurements found roughly 10–14 µs of additional host submission time per full linear call for most tested shapes when using the checked API instead of an unchecked launcher; the final implementation retains validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The operator contract is documented in its docstring; no user-facing configuration changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Local results and their limits are reported above; isolated end-to-end performance remains unverified.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Cosmos-Dreams rollout-owned prefix K/V buffer
issues.body:
## Motivation

Every denoise step, each layer concatenated `[text | history]` and then `[prefix | chunk]`, and every commit re-allocated the whole history. That is 2 full K/V history copies per layer per step plus an O(T) copy per commit.

## Changes

- `PrefixKVHistory` (cosmos_dreams.py): per-layer `[text | history | chunk scratch]` buffers owned by the rollout. Indexing returns history views, so it works anywhere a `list[KVPair]` history is read.
- The transformer writes the chunk's K/V into the scratch rows and attends to a view, so no history copy per step. `_joint_attention` takes `chunk_in_prefix` and keeps its old signature.
- `append_kv_history` appends in place for the buffer, with the same sink + window eviction and the same window check.
- Rollout creates the buffer at the first commit. Its initial capacity is `sink + window + chunk` frames, capped at the request's latent frame count so short requests do not over-reserve. The buffer grows on demand if needed. Frustum `SelectedHistory` and plain lists still work and take a single-copy path via `_prefix_kv`.

## Tests

Added `TestCosmosDreamsPrefixBuffer` (Modal CPU): buffer contents are bitwise equal to `append_kv_history` over mixed append sizes (full, sliding, sink+window, preallocated capacity), initial-block-over-window is rejected, and `_joint_attention` with `chunk_in_prefix` is bitwise equal to the concat path. `test_cosmos_dreams.py`: 61 passed, 1 skipped on Modal CPU. The 3 `test_offloaded_vae_uses_serial_decode` subtests fail identically on main in the CPU env (55 passed, same 3 failures on main).

## Benchmark

Real checkpoint (`nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual`), Modal L40S, base 9f6678aa3d vs this branch. 81 frames (21 latent), 480x640, seed 1, fixed synthetic input image, no actions, full-history default profile. 1 cold warmup run discarded, then 10 warm runs per variant, alternating. Full per-run data and tests are in the comment below.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Rollout stage, mean (s) | 6.837 (sd 0.065) | 6.718 (sd 0.079) |
| Peak memory (MB) | 30960 | 29924 |
| Output mp4 md5 | identical across all 20 runs | identical across all 20 runs |

The rollout is 1.7% faster (95% CI 0.7% to 2.7%; Welch p = 0.0018, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0036). That is statistically significant but small at this size (short history, small chunk). Peak memory is about 1 GB lower. Caveats: noise input and null actions, one resolution and GPU, full-history profile only, runs share a container.

Earlier synthetic microbenchmark (L4, 12 layers, 16 heads / 4 KV heads, head dim 128, 512 text tokens, 256 tokens per frame, chunk of 4 frames, 4 denoise steps, framewise commits, QK norm and RoPE stubbed, plain SDPA): 1.04x to 1.08x, outputs bitwise equal, with gains growing with history length and shrinking as chunk size grows. Not a substitute for the real-checkpoint numbers above.

`cosmos3_sim_auto.py` and `nomas_kv_cache.py` are not touched.

issues.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/nomas: Fuse VAE QK normalization and MRoPE epilogue
issues.body:
## Motivation

The Nomas PixelUMM VAE computes Q/K mean squares with ATen and then runs three compiled pointwise kernels for normalization and three-axis rotary embedding. Those three kernels are repeated 864 times in the profiled 1280×704×121 decode.

This change fuses the pointwise epilogue into one Triton kernel while retaining the ATen reductions, existing chunking and output-copy behavior. It preserves the actual Parameter-backed compiled reference's FP32 multiply/FMA rounding. A per-signature `BitExactFusionGate` verifies the result before retaining the fast path. The existing head-64, autograd/compiler and unsupported-layout paths remain available. The fusion is eligible for BF16 head-128 inputs with rotary sections `(64,32,32)` on SM100+; model performance below is measured on SM103 only.

This is independent of [#49308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49308), which changes the DiT mean-square reduction. This branch starts directly from the frozen main and contains no DiT change or new configuration flag.

- Main baseline: `5325cfabd757819e2e01bb7eb3b28c5b39b8cec9`.
- PR head: `aef7b894a610f6c04fe43d00ea9decca2ab1f718`.
- Native vLLM-Omni reference: `725c1c9acd108d9f5248bd937489f19a2c560205`.

## Accuracy and cleanup

The exact committed head passes 14 focused operator cases and one model-wrapper test against the actual Parameter-backed compiled reference. The cases cover chunk views with storage offsets and batch gaps, extreme amplitudes, changed inputs during CUDA Graph replay, invalid mean shapes, activation on the real head-128 wrapper and head-64 fallback.

Final-head quality comprises **18 explicit main/PR request pairs and 1,962 frame comparisons**: 640×352×49 seed42; 1280×704×121 seeds42/123/2026 in lossless mode on one GPU; and the same high-resolution seed42 workload in high mode on one GPU and lossless mode with Ulysses2. Every native BF16 byte and decoded pixel matches the corresponding main configuration. Each configuration includes short/long/short request reuse. The high and two-GPU checks establish compatibility only; their latency is not claimed here.

The 12 one-GPU initial quality requests also audit actual fusion activation: 144 calls per small-video request and 864 per large-video request, with verified signatures and no disabled gate. Before/after cleanup has six additional exact native-byte/pixel pairs at both resolutions.

The existing baseline test comparing its compiled epilogue to an unfused eager expression already fails for two larger layouts with this Torch runtime. Those assertions are unchanged. This PR preserves the actual compiled baseline rounding and includes the separate diagnostic in the evidence bundle.

The six-file diff was reviewed and simplified before the cleanup and final-head tests. Cleanup follows the actual source/review patterns in [#40265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40265), [#48366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48366) and [#49189](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49189). It removes redundant test temporaries and keeps one public entry point, focused eligibility checks and the existing verification utility. The fused-kernel inventory is updated. Ruff, isort, `git diff --check`, Mint validation and broken-link checks pass.

## Final-head performance

Hardware: the same physical NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC for all arms. Native Hy-Nomas, BF16, 1280×704, 121 frames, 24 FPS, 8 steps, CFG1, flow shift5, seed42, CPU RNG, batch/concurrency1, no offload. Both SGLang arms disable full-model compilation and BCG while retaining pre-existing compiled pointwise epilogues and the same numerical-policy defaults. cuDNN TF32 and BF16 reduced-precision reductions are allowed; exactness means preservation of this native main configuration.

A/A uses two independent main processes with two warmups and five measured requests each. Full per-prompt observed ranges are 0.4252% and 0.4193%, below the preregistered 0.5% bound.

| Arm | E2E median / p95 (s) | Denoise median (ms, async diagnostic) | Peak reserved (MiB) | Measured requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main `5325cfabd7` | 13.2703 / 13.3314 | 7587.42 | 51656 | 30 |
| PR `aef7b894a6` | 13.0499 / 13.1716 | 7587.57 | 51656 | 30 |

Three new ABBA rounds give paired geometric speedup **1.016975×**, or **1.6692% lower E2E latency**. The round-cluster bootstrap 95% interval is [1.014385×, 1.020799×]. These are three independent rounds, not sixty independent experiments. All 60 measured and 24 warmup outputs match per prompt. The source/configuration audit verifies all 84 records against the clean committed SHAs and fixed GPU UUID.

Process initialization: 37.83–39.56s. First/second warmup generation: 21.17–22.12s / 12.98–13.35s. Compiler caches are retained, so these are not fresh-container cold-start measurements.

| Arm | E2E median / p95 (s) | Denoise median (ms, async diagnostic) | Peak reserved (MiB) | Measured requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before cleanup | 12.9795 / 13.0209 | 7595.35 | 51656 | 20 |
| After cleanup (runtime/tests identical to final head) | 12.9544 / 12.9872 | 7587.22 | 51656 | 20 |

Two independent cleanup ABBA rounds give before/after **1.002597×**, or after-latency change **-0.2591%**. Overall and every round/prompt pair stay inside the fixed 0.5% neutrality bound; all 40 measured and 16 warmup outputs match. No confidence interval is inferred from two rounds. The final commit adds documentation to this exact cleaned runtime/test tree.

The timer includes native generation and frame materialization, excluding hashing, array saving and video encoding. Profiling, verification hooks, archive I/O and downloads are excluded from latency measurements. This is offline latency; no HTTP throughput claim is made. Asynchronous denoise-stage metrics are diagnostics rather than synchronized GPU time.

## Native Omni reference and quality limits

| Same workload/GPU | E2E median / p95 (s) | Measured requests | Allocated / reserved peak (MiB, separate attribution) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Native Omni `725c1c9acd` | 19.5245 / 19.8001 | 10, two independent processes | 59764.14 / 64064 |

The supplied native Hy-Nomas deploy configuration requires `enforce_eager=True`; full transformer compilation is unsupported at this revision. Native compiled FlexAttention remains enabled. The separate environment and wheel pins are recorded, including the required private cuDNN runtime. The zero-valued denoise output metric is a placeholder, not measured zero. Separate synchronized attribution gives 10164.40ms across eight denoise steps plus 1273.53ms for the clean KV-cache commit forward; these values are excluded from the latency samples.

Effective BF16 weights (all 3,082 loaded tensors), tokens, masks, initial noise and timesteps were audited across the frameworks. Outputs nevertheless differ visibly. For the 1280×704×121 seed42 baseline, short/long mean all-frame SSIM is 0.821916/0.818989 and PSNR is 24.0311/24.8243dB. Seed2026's long prompt is worse: SSIM0.581538, PSNR19.3859dB, minimum frame SSIM0.552361 at frame56. These rows are reference context and **do not qualify as cross-framework performance wins**. The PR's accepted improvement is against frozen SGLang main. Every frozen matrix row and the current result overlay, including pending/failed cases, are in the bundle.

## Matched profile and actual output media

Both separate final-head traces use synchronized stage profiling. Every GPU kernel is assigned once to its stage. DiT keeps all 28,990 kernel calls, with every per-kernel count unchanged. VAE decode drops from **10,262 to 8,534 calls**: 2,592 old pointwise calls become 864 `_qk_norm_mrope_kernel` calls. Their summed GPU duration is 360.38ms →69.76ms. The VAE stage span is 4077.86ms →3815.11ms. All other kernel call counts are unchanged. These trace durations explain the mechanism; they are not latency samples.

Trace SHA256: main `412e720e8fa0ee8bb7110ef5e87ea6cb209af71656555fa4f9c4344760b3cc73`; final `d2d41f2ebece12b36e673a13421577979617216766dd2dbf795c49f064e1f4ce`. [Full stage/kernel report](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/nomas-vae-final-gpu-profile-digest-v1.json).

The following are actual main/final-head videos, Hy-Nomas BF16, one B300, 1280×704×121, 8 steps, CFG1, seed123. Each montage shows frames0/60/120 at 0/2.5/5 seconds. Every native byte and decoded pixel agrees.

![Actual main and PR short-prompt video frames at 0, 2.5 and 5 seconds](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/main-vs-final-00-short-1280x704-f121-seed123.png)

Short prompt: [main video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/main-00-short-1280x704-f121-seed123.mp4) · [PR video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/final-00-short-1280x704-f121-seed123.mp4).

![Actual main and PR long-prompt video frames at 0, 2.5 and 5 seconds](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/main-vs-final-01-long-1280x704-f121-seed123.png)

Long prompt: [main video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/main-01-long-1280x704-f121-seed123.mp4) · [PR video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/final-01-long-1280x704-f121-seed123.mp4).

## Reproduction and scope

[Commands and environment setup](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/nomas-vae-reproduction.txt) · [Original measurements, scripts, frozen matrix and audits](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/nomas-vae-reproduction-and-results.tar.gz) · [Bundle hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/nomas-vae-reproduction-and-results-manifest.json) · [Media provenance](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-nomas-vae-rope-evidence-20261109/nomas-vae-final-media-provenance.json).

issues.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/nomas: Fuse exact head-128 mean-square reduction
issues.body:
## Motivation

Nomas calls its Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE wrapper repeatedly during denoising. The existing wrapper materializes the BF16 input as FP32, squares it, and calls ATen mean before its compiled normalization/rotation epilogue. On a B300, the cast/square/reduction chain is visible in the full-model profile.

This change replaces that reduction with one kernel for supported BF16 head-128 layouts. It extracts and reuses the ordered reduction already used by the in-tree bit-exact RMSNorm kernels. The existing compiled epilogue stays in place, retaining its rounding. A per-signature BitExactFusionGate verifies the reduction against ATen; unsupported layouts, camera head-64, autograd and other existing fallback conditions keep their reference paths.

Baseline: `5325cfabd757819e2e01bb7eb3b28c5b39b8cec9`.
PR head: `4f25dde0bf22a3fe194d03c2782e515341ece64f`.
Native vLLM-Omni reference: `725c1c9acd108d9f5248bd937489f19a2c560205`.

## Accuracy Tests

The shared ordered-reduction refactor passed 78 relevant operator tests. One additional Nomas test covers the actual compiled epilogue, verified fusion activation and camera head-64 fallback. Operator tests cover packed views, batched inputs, extreme amplitudes, mutable-input CUDA Graph replay and a compiled custom-op call.

Before/after cleanup quality at 640×352×49 and 1280×704×121, seed 42, matched every native BF16 output element and every decoded pixel, including short/long/short request reuse. The exact committed head additionally matches main at 640×352×121 (seed 42), 1280×704×121 (seeds 123/2026 on one GPU, seed 42 with Ulysses 2), and 1280×704×241 with two events and Ulysses 2/4 (seed 42). These final-head checks comprise 12 main/PR case pairs and 1,932 all-frame comparisons; all native tensors and pixels match. Every repeated-request pixel check also passes.

The existing `test_fused_qk_norm_rope_and_modulate_cast_are_bitwise_exact` also exposes a difference between the baseline compiled epilogue and the unfused eager expression with this Torch runtime. This PR retains that compiled epilogue and tests against actual baseline behavior; it does not loosen the existing assertion or claim to fix that separate issue.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, same physical GPU for each arm. Workload: native Hy-Nomas, BF16, 1280×704, 121 frames, 8 steps, CFG 1, flow shift 5, seed 42, CPU RNG, batch/concurrency 1, no offload. Full-model torch.compile and BCG are disabled in both SGLang arms; pre-existing pointwise compilation is retained.

Both SGLang arms retain the same native numerical-policy defaults: cuDNN TF32 and BF16 reduced-precision reductions are allowed. The lossless claim means exact preservation of this main configuration, not a new strict-FP32 library contract. The Omni worker likewise reports cuDNN TF32 and BF16 reduced-precision reduction allowed; matmul TF32 is disabled and float32 matmul precision is `highest`. These observed policy flags are recorded with the separate native attribution trace.

A/A: two independent processes, two warmups and five measured requests each. Per-prompt CV <=0.18%; full observed range <=0.47%.

| Final-head comparison | E2E median / p95 (s) | Denoise median (ms, async diagnostic) | Peak reserved (MiB) | Measured requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main `5325cfabd7` | 13.2316 / 13.2721 | 7588.19 | 51656 | 30 |
| PR `4f25dde0bf` | 12.9954 / 13.0460 | 7350.29 | 51554 | 30 |

Three independent ABBA rounds give paired geometric speedup **1.017632×**, or **1.7326% lower E2E latency**. The round-cluster bootstrap 95% interval is [1.016757×, 1.018689×]; there are three independent rounds, not sixty independent experiments. All 60 measured outputs and 24 warmup outputs match per prompt. Every record uses the same physical GPU and an unchanged clean source tree at the stated SHA. issues.title: [sglang-miles] [Diffusion] Let a rollout request skip the VAE decode
issues.body:
## Motivation

Data-free DMD2 in miles-diffusion (radixark/miles_diffusion#343) trains only on the rollout trajectory: the student's input and x0 prediction from `dit_trajectory`, and the cond from `denoising_env`. With no reward model, nothing reads the decoded media of a training rollout. Every rollout request still runs the VAE decode (video and, for MiniMax H3, audio) and ships the decoded video. For H3 at 768p 16:9 5 s that is 124×768×1344×3 B = 384 MB per sample even as `uint8`, about 123 GB per 320-sample rollout through HTTP and msgpack.

## Modifications

- `RolloutRequest` / `SamplingParams`: `rollout_return_generated_output`, default `True` (no behavior change). It is a `SamplingParams` field without `batch_sig_exclude`, so requests that decode and requests that don't are never batched together.
- `rollout_output_without_decode` (`stages/decoding.py`): the `OutputBatch` with the rollout trajectory, trajectory timesteps / latents, metrics and usage, and no media.
- `DecodingStage.forward` and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage.forward` return it first thing when the field is `False`, before loading or running a VAE. H3's `verify_output` accepts that output (no media, a rollout trajectory) and still rejects any other empty output.
- `rollout_generate` rejects a request with the field `False` whose output came back decoded anyway (400). Decoding stages that override `forward` without the check (LTX-2, Cosmos3, MOVA, ...) would otherwise decode silently; they can opt in the same way. `_build_response` takes the response count from `num_outputs_per_prompt` when there is no output.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-H3 (t2va, 2×B200 TP2, 768p 16:9 4 s = 1344×768 / 107 frames, 4 steps, `ode`, seed 1234, `rollout_video_dtype=uint8`, `rollout_return_dit_trajectory` and `rollout_return_denoising_env` on), on a tree with this commit and #46544 (audio in the response) on top of `sglang-miles` 2a2fb7310; the two touch separate response fields:

- With `rollout_return_generated_output=False`, `dit_trajectory` (latents `[5, 32256, 96]`, timesteps, sigmas, step indices), `denoising_env` (9 tensors) and `rollout_log_probs` are bitwise equal to the decoded request's; `generated_output` is `None`.
- With the default, the decoded request is unchanged: against `sglang-miles` 2a2fb7310 on the same request, the decoded video, `dit_trajectory`, `denoising_env` and `rollout_log_probs` are bitwise equal.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup, after one warm-up request:

| | decode on (6 runs) | `rollout_return_generated_output=False` (4 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` | 1.27 s | 0.0000 s |
| `inference_time_s` | 5.92-5.94 s | 4.66-4.67 s |
| response body | 396.2 MB | 63.7 MB |
| client wall time | 8.2-11.6 s | 5.6-7.0 s |

The remaining 63.7 MB is the full 5-latent trajectory; a DMD2 request that stops at a step and returns two latents ships about 25 MB.

## Tests

- `test_rollout_api.py`:
  - the field reaches the pipeline request (`Req`), and defaults to `True`;
  - `DecodingStage` and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` return the request's trajectory without touching the VAE;
  - H3's output verification accepts the trajectory-only output and still rejects an empty output without a rollout trajectory;
  - a response without output has one entry per requested output, with the trajectory sliced per sample.
- 44 passed in `test_rollout_api.py`; 443 passed across the 29 unit files that touch decoding, H3, rollout and sampling params. `pre-commit run` on the changed files is clean.

issues.title: [Doc] diffusion: Fix documented snippets that cannot load a model
issues.body:
Three copy-pasteable snippets that build a generator fail before producing any video: two import a name that does not exist, and one calls `from_pretrained` in a way that cannot set the model path.

### 1. `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LongLive/LongLive-2.0.mdx` (Multi-shot section)

```python
from sglang import DiffGenerator
```

`DiffGenerator` is not exported by the top-level `sglang` package: it is absent from `__all__` in `python/sglang/__init__.py`, and that module defines no `__getattr__`, so the import raises `ImportError`.

It is exported by `sglang.multimodal_gen` (`__all__ = ["DiffGenerator", "PipelineConfig", "SamplingParams"]`), which is how every other diffusion page imports it (`Kandinsky6.mdx`, `Kandinsky6-SR.mdx`, `progressive_resolution.mdx`, `plugin.mdx`).

### 2. `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/support_new_models.mdx` (Implement the Pieces, step 1)

```python
from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.sample.sampling_params import ImageSamplingParams
```

There is no `ImageSamplingParams` class. That module defines `SamplingParams`, `SkipSoftmaxParams` and `CacheParams`, and every image pipeline in the tree subclasses `SamplingParams` (`zimage.py`, `qwenimage.py`, `ernie_image.py`, `longcat_image.py`, `ming_image.py`, ...). The same page refers to `SamplingParams` elsewhere.

### 3. `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LongLive/LongLive-2.0.mdx` (same snippet, next line)

```python
gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained("Rabinovich/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers")
```

The signature is `from_pretrained(cls, local_mode: bool = True, **kwargs)` (`multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/diffusion_generator.py`). The positional string binds to `local_mode`, so `model_path` is never set and `ServerArgs.from_kwargs()` gets no model. Every other page passes it by keyword (`model_path=...` in `progressive_resolution.mdx`, `Kandinsky6.mdx`, `HY-Nomas.mdx`, `multimodal_gen/README.md`).

The same two mistakes appear in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (lines 31-32); corrected there too.

### Change

Snippets now import symbols that exist and pass `model_path=` by keyword. Docs and comments only; no code or test change.

issues.body:
## Motivation

The model cookbooks document each realtime model's `init` fields and event kinds. The parts every realtime pipeline shares are not written down anywhere, and a client author has to read `realtime_video_api.py` and `realtime_output_adapter.py` to find them:

- client messages must be binary MessagePack frames;
- a frame batch arrives either as one `frame_batch` message or as a `frame_batch_header` followed by a raw payload message;
- `chunk_stats` follows each chunk;
- an event applies to the chunk after the one being generated, and frame batches echo the `event_id` of the latest event their chunk sampled;
- what happens on an invalid `init`, an invalid event, `max_chunks`, a busy GPU slot, and a client disconnect.

## Modifications

Add a "Session Protocol" section to `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/realtime_models.mdx`, between "Supported Realtime Pipelines" and "Causal Cache Controls". It describes the current behavior on `main`, checked against the code:

- `FRAME_BATCH_PACK_OFFLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024` decides `frame_batch` vs `frame_batch_header` + payload, and `session.output_lock` keeps the header and its payload adjacent;
- `_send_output_and_log` sends `chunk_stats` after the chunk's frames;
- all four adapters (LingBot World, SANA-WM, HY-Nomas, Cosmos-Dreams) return `latest_sampled_event_id` from `get_realtime_event_id`;
- HY-Nomas (`end` event) and SANA-WM (a chunk with no frames) end a session by setting `max_chunks`, which closes with `1000` `generation complete`.

## Motivation

Add support for the official [Hy-Nomas](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-Nomas) distilled INT8 DiT and PixelUMM FP8 VAE checkpoints to the existing Nomas pipeline introduced in #46124.

The INT8 DiT stores quantized weights and retains BF16 linear computation. The FP8 VAE uses block-scaled Triton FP8 GEMM.

## Modifications

- Validate official checkpoint metadata, layer manifests, tensor shapes and dtypes before loading.
- Load groupwise INT8 DiT weights through the parallel linear loaders, dequantize in FP32 for BF16 computation, and preserve FP32 scales across component moves.
- Load the FP8 VAE on meta, replace its 180 selected decoder projections, and stream weights through the existing VAE loader.
- Match the official SM89 activation quantization using 128×128 blocks and reuse the existing Triton block FP8 GEMM.
- Let the VAE model declare quantized projections and unused encoder weights while retaining strict decoder validation.
- Extend Nomas tests to cover checkpoint validation, serialization, parallel loading, quantized computation and dtype preservation


## Accuracy Tests

### Demo video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d2c514c-c3d8-4c0a-b999-b294f70bdd75



### Real-weight generation and reference comparison

Generated a video through the public DiffGenerator API on one RTX 4090 D with the official INT8 DiT, FP8 VAE and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct text encoder.

Configuration: 352×640, 40 frames, 24 fps, 8 Euler steps, guidance scale 1, seed 42, structured JSON caption, and CPU offload for all three components.

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| SGLang DiT replay vs. captured pipeline | All 8 predictions bitwise identical; all 775 scales remain FP32 |
| Official DiT vs. SGLang with shared text and main attention implementations | All 8 predictions and final latent bitwise identical |
| Video pixels using each implementation's attention and FP8 GEMM paths | PSNR 26.37 dB; mean SSIM 0.8277 |
| Video pixels with shared DiT attention, Triton vs. official CUTLASS VAE | PSNR 42.64 dB; mean SSIM 0.9920 |
| Video pixels with shared DiT attention and test-only official CUTLASS VAE linears | Bitwise identical |
| Standalone SGLang VAE replay vs. captured pipeline | Bitwise identical |

Pixel metrics are computed before MP4 encoding. PSNR uses raw outputs with data range 2; SSIM uses outputs normalized and clipped to [0, 1]. Shared-backend substitutions are for validation only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Test with 1 single 4090D, output 40 frames at 24 fps.

Smoke measurement with the configuration above:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Generation time | 69.52 s |
| Peak allocated GPU memory | 15,317 MiB |
| Peak reserved GPU memory | 16,158 MiB |

This measurement includes component transfers and cold execution. It is not a comparative performance benchmark.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Nomas camera attention reads each frame's value directly when camera_chunk_size is 1
issues.body:
## Summary

When `camera_chunk_size == 1` (the value in the released Hy-Nomas `transformer/config.json`), each camera chunk is one latent frame, so the softmax in `NomasCameraAttention` runs over a single key and equals 1.0. The output for every token is just the value vector of its frame, independent of q and k.

This PR takes that path directly: it skips the `img_attn_q` GEMM, the q/k RMSNorm + RoPE and the per-frame SDPA launches, and gathers `v` by frame index (with `token_offset` for sequence-parallel slices). Other chunk sizes use the old code unchanged. The change is 7 lines in `nomas.py` (`git diff -w`); the rest of the diff is re-indentation of the old path into the `else`.

Scope: this only runs for requests that carry camera poses (`norm_extrinsics`). Requests without a camera never reach this module.

## Evidence

Real Hy-Nomas DiT weights loaded from the assembled checkpoint (0 missing / 0 unexpected keys), H100, 352x640, one 10-latent segment of 8 steps, DiT only, random text embeddings, median of several runs:

| | original | this PR | bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|---|
| hist 0 | 1341 ms | 1237 ms (-8%) | yes |
| hist 3 | 1460 ms | 1271 ms (-13%) | yes |
| hist 8 | 1543 ms | 1322 ms (-14%) | yes |

A second container (slower host CPU) showed larger gains for the same comparison: 1858 -> 1370 ms (-26%) at hist 0, 1920 -> 1438 ms (-25%) at hist 3, 2299 -> 1814 ms (-21%) at hist 3 with action windows. The forward issues about 8k kernel launches and the GPU is idle roughly half the time, so the gain scales with how launch-bound the host is. Absolute numbers differ between containers; only compare within a table.

## Tests

`test_camera_chunk_of_one_reads_each_frames_value_without_attention` in `test_nomas.py`: builds the expected output with real SDPA over random q/k (one key per frame), checks the module matches it, checks a slice that starts mid-frame, and fails if `img_attn_q` is called.

- main: fails (`a one-key softmax needs no query`), Modal CPU.
- This PR: **not run on the final tree** (CPU or CUDA unit tests). Bitwise equality was checked on real weights in the benchmark above.

## Review

An independent review pass found no correctness issue. Optional follow-ups it suggested: a `has_camera` tensor case in the test, and a comment that the shortcut relies on `chunk_size == 1`.

## Not checked

- No end-to-end camera request, only the DiT.
- Fixed-tree CPU and CUDA unit tests not run (see above).
- TP/SP multi-rank run not done; the slice test covers the `token_offset` path on one rank.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Nomas KV budget counts freed cached memory, reject SP-indivisible segments up front
issues.body:
## Summary

Fixes #47515. Two small bug fixes in the Hy-Nomas pipeline.

- `_free_bytes` now adds `memory_reserved - memory_allocated` (same correction as `qwen_image21._cache_fits`), so memory the allocator holds from an earlier request counts as available. Before, the KV budget came out too low, which caused false `Nomas KV requires ...` errors offline and early eviction in realtime.
- `NomasInputValidationStage` now rejects a segment whose video tokens (`latent_frames * H/32 * W/32`) are not divisible by the Ulysses degree, at request time. Before, `local_token_range` raised deep in the DiT, after text encoding and mid-session in realtime. Realtime flush chunks (1 latent frame, never run through the DiT) are exempt.

## Tests

Two tests added to the existing `test_nomas.py` (the SP one is parametrized: 13 frames ok, 17 frames rejected, flush chunk ok). Run on Modal CPU, targeted files only.

| | B1 test | SP test |
|---|---|---|
| main | fails: `assert 10 == 40` | 17 frames fails: `DID NOT RAISE ValueError` |
| this PR | passes | passes |

- `test_nomas.py` + `test_nomas_realtime.py` on this PR: 42 passed, 11 skipped (CUDA-only).
- Removing the flush exemption makes the flush case fail, so that test guards it.

## Review

An independent review pass found the flush-chunk rejection in my first version of the SP check. Fixed and covered by the flush test case. It also noted that the validation stage running with model parallel initialized on real workers is not covered by the unit test.

## Not checked

- No GPU end-to-end run. Both fixes are exact and covered on CPU; an SP=2 smoke run would confirm the validation stage on real workers.
- `test_nomas_parallel.py` not run (multi-process).
- Formatter not run locally.

issues.title: [Refactor] bcg: Record graph breaks at capture without running them
issues.body:
Needs #46718, now merged.

- While a breakable CUDA graph captures, `eager_on_graph` now ends the segment, runs the barrier and the break's `capture_stub` if it has one, records the call, and starts the next segment. The break body no longer runs at capture: its inputs come from segments that have not run yet, so running it there only wrote values nothing reads, and ran collectives and host syncs on them.
- Every break already writes into buffers or holders its caller prepares and returns `None`. The wrapper now asserts `None` at replay and in eager runs, and `_copy_output`, which copied each replay's fresh return value into the output captured at capture time, is removed.
- `capture_stub` stays for host setup that a later captured segment reads: the DeepSeek V4 late-layer tail enter and exit, the tail source KV layer id (#46718), and the Nemotron-H shared-expert side graph. Stubs that only fill outputs no longer do anything useful and are left for a follow-up cleanup.
- The diffusion BCG warmup now runs with the BCG flag on, so it takes the branches the capture records and allocates what the capture expects instead of relying on the capture pass to run each break once.
- The DeepSeek V4 tail enter and exit breaks no longer take a sentinel tensor: they returned it only to keep the break in the replay sequence, and a break now returns `None`.
- Tests: the break tests use caller buffers, and `test_eager_on_graph.py` checks that the capture pass records breaks without running them and that a break returning a value fails (the XPU and multimodal break tests follow the same shape).
- GPU runs at this head on B300 and GB300 pass: `test_breakable_cuda_graph.py`, `test_bcg_with_lora.py`, `test_bcg_with_speculative_decoding.py`, `test_dp_attention_bcg_kl.py`, `test_lora_moe_prefill_cuda_graph.py`, `test_mamba_cache_kl.py`, `test_decoder_tail_moe_bound.py`, `test_deepseek_dual_stream_outputs.py`, the dense, MLA, GDN, SWA and DeepSeek V4 attention unit tests, the DeepSeek V4 Flash FP4 tests, the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash bounded-tail and encoder BCG tests, the Z-Image Turbo BCG tests (single GPU and TP 2), and the multimodal unit tests. `test_paged_experts.py` (GPTQ class), `test_glm53_cp_bcg_dflash.py` (KV transfer) and two `test_nomas.py` cases fail the same way on main.
